working_title: Southwest Ireland's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Kerry and Clare for UK Visitors
angle: Rather than a bucket-list overview, this post maps a realistic self-drive loop through southwest Ireland's links corridor for regular club golfers flying from the UK, covering which courses to prioritise, how to sequence the trip logistically, and what to watch out for when booking. The tone is practical and opinionated, not reverential.
research_notes:
- Southwest Ireland (Kerry and Clare) has more than 50 golf courses; the greatest concentration of championship links is along this stretch of coast (Golf Ireland figure cited widely)
- Key courses on the circuit: Ballybunion Old Course (Co. Kerry, founded 1893, designed Robert Trent Jones Sr.), Lahinch Old Course (Co. Clare, founded 1892, originally Old Tom Morris, redesigned Alister MacKenzie), Waterville (Co. Kerry, Ring of Kerry, remote links), Tralee (designed Arnold Palmer, described as his first European course), Dooks (golf played there since 1889, Dingle Bay), Old Head Golf Links near Kinsale (216-acre/220-acre headland peninsula jutting into Atlantic)
- Doonbeg/Trump International Golf Links (Co. Clare, Greg Norman design, 16 holes with Atlantic views)
- Adare Manor parkland course (Co. Limerick, Tom Fazio redesign, reopened 2017) confirmed host of 2027 Ryder Cup, good anchor base at start of trip
- Logical routing from Shannon Airport: Lahinch 45 mins, Ballybunion 90 mins, Waterville under 3 hours via Ring of Kerry
- The Wild Atlantic Way driving route connects many courses in a natural touring corridor
- September described as 'one of the most pleasant months in Ireland' for links golf; visitor tee times at some clubs reduce from mid-October
- Top clubs (Ballybunion, Lahinch, Old Head) book out far in advance; booking direct often shows 'Sold Out' when specialist operators may still have availability
- Many links courses do not allow buggies or restrict use; walkers should be prepared; caddies recommended at championship venues
- A car is essential for exploring rural courses; Shannon and Kerry Airports are the main entry points, Cork also an option
- Suggested trip length: 4–7 days for southwest focus; anything shorter means giving up courses you shouldn't have to
- 2026 golf calendar note: Walker Cup at Lahinch (September 5–6); Amgen Irish Open at Trump Doonbeg (September 10–13) — worth knowing for tee-time availability around those dates
- Walker Cup and Irish Open dates mean tee-time availability around September 5–13 at Lahinch and Doonbeg may be tighter than usual
must_avoid:
- No fabricated green fees or specific prices (none confirmed in research)
- No invented quotes from pros or reviewers about specific holes
- No gambling or betting content
- No medical/injury advice beyond generic warm-up mentions
- No financial advice on affordability of the trip
- Do not duplicate the East Lothian (Scotland) or Wales links posts already published
- Northern Ireland (Royal County Down, Royal Portrush) is a distinct destination; do not conflate with southwest Ireland or blend into the same post
- Do not add any note about affiliate link omissions in the post body; if no approved partners exist for Irish golf operators, simply mention operators informationally with no link and no editorial comment about it
- No em dashes anywhere in the post
